old: - Treatment: IMMEDIATE surgical debridement + broad-spectrum IV antibiotics (pip-tazo or carbapenems + clindamycin for toxin suppression); do NOT delay surgery for imaging
new: - Treatment: urgent surgical debridement plus empiric MRSA-active and broad gram-negative/anaerobic therapy; an IDSA example is linezolid plus a carbapenem. Use the loaded component regimen and organ guidance. Do not delay surgery for imaging.
(legacy snapshot reconciled against IDSA 2014 and loaded UCSF guidance)

old: - Streptococcal etiology (Groups A, B, C, G) — no MRSA coverage needed
new: - Typical mild nonpurulent disease needs streptococcal coverage; MRSA-active coverage is conditional on risk/severity rather than universally unnecessary.

old: extend to 14 days if slow improvement
new: extend if not improved; reassess diagnosis, source control and severity rather than default to 14 days

old: adults; NOT pregnant women or children <8 years
new: adult regimen; pediatric short-course eligibility is disease-specific, including all-age high-risk prophylaxis; pregnancy decisions require individualized assessment
- High-risk beta-lactam allergy: assess phenotype and consult pediatric allergy/ASP guidance. Do not use TMP-SMX as a routine AOM alternative; resistance and pathogen coverage matter.
ascitic PMN ≥250/mm3 after excluding a secondary intra-abdominal source; culture may be negative and is not required

old: - Secondary prophylaxis (after SBP): norfloxacin 400 mg/day indefinitely
new: - Secondary prophylaxis: select a locally available source-supported regimen such as daily TMP-SMX after individual risk review; do not assume US availability of norfloxacin.

old:
- TMP-SMX DS × 14 days (if susceptibility known) OR
- Oral beta-lactam × 10-14 days (less efficacious)
new: - Duration reconciliation: IDSA 2025 suggests 7 days effective non-fluoroquinolone therapy for eligible improving cUTI/pyelonephritis. Short-course evidence has important exclusions; pregnancy pyelonephritis remains 14 days and suspected prostatitis/abscess/obstruction requires separate selection.
individualize effective duration and catheter/source control; do not apply an automatic 7-14-day rule to all patients

old: - Target duration: 7-10 days for most infections; shorter durations validated for CAP, UTI, peritonitis
new: - Duration: use the infection-specific effective course, source control, cultures and clinical response; do not apply an automatic 7-10-day course to every sepsis syndrome. Reassess daily for narrowing and stopping.
